result.summary: Converts walletprocesspsbt to accept its four existing settings (sign, sighashtype, bip32derivs, finalize) inside a single options dictionary as its second parameter while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing positional and named calls. Updates the RPC framework to support distinct declared types per parameter alias and describes multi-type parameters with oneOf in OpenRPC schema output.
result.problem: walletprocesspsbt takes four positional parameters after the PSBT, most of which are booleans, making calls error-prone and forcing any newly added settings (such as in PR 32857) to become additional positional arguments. The RPC framework also lacked support for assigning different types to different parameter aliases, preventing an options object from replacing legacy positional arguments without breaking backwards compatibility.
evidence: PR description: walletprocesspsbt takes four settings after the PSBT, three of them booleans, so a positional call reads walletprocesspsbt "psbt" true "ALL" true false, and each new setting becomes one more positional parameter (#32857 would add a sixth).
Description notes this picks up closed PR #24963 with fixes for OpenRPC schema generation and mixed positional/named argument parsing.
result.scope_notes: Modifies shared RPC argument parsing mechanisms (alias type resolution, OpenRPC schemas, and named argument transformation) in addition to walletprocesspsbt itself.
result.card: Converts walletprocesspsbt to take an options dictionary as its second argument while preserving backwards compatibility for callers using the legacy positional boolean and string parameters. Today, walletprocesspsbt requires up to four trailing positional parameters, making invocations unwieldy and requiring any new functionality (such as in PR 32857) to append yet another positional parameter. The change also enhances the core RPC framework to support distinct types per parameter alias and updates OpenRPC schema generation. Unblocks adding new settings cleanly to walletprocesspsbt without growing the positional argument list.

risk.why: Mistakes in RPC parameter transformation and type validation could break client compatibility or cause valid RPC calls to be erroneously rejected.
